top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a distinct invention: magic-wavelength trapping removes the lattice Stark shift while Lamb-Dicke confinement lets many neutral atoms be interrogated at once, bringing uncertainty to about 1e-18, and independent laboratories have reproduced and surpassed it. Katori and Ye are a complete two-name allocation with no forced third name, and the citation can name the lattice clock and magic-wavelength trapping without the SI redefinition, separating it from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. P002 ranks second: Kane-Mele topological insulators are conceptually more fundamental, but crediting the HgTe observation without the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal (Zhang died in 2018) is a structural credit defect. An award is preferable to no award.
